bull_bear.body:
- Stock split + bonus done to boost liquidity / shareholder count (~11,000 → ~25,000; target 100k-150k).
- No equity dilution intended for capex; promoter willing to infuse unsecured loans; rights issue preferred over preferential/private placement if needed.
- Acquisition appetite continues (FDF/peptide) but discretionary.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Working capital:** receivables ~200+ days (mgmt benchmark ~180 for API; admits ~130-140 average); ~INR 100 cr receivables ≈ 60% of sales; consol operating cash flow -INR 47 cr. New strict 120-day stop-supply policy; positive CF promised by FY27-end — KEY proof point.
- **Legacy bad-ish receivable:** lost a distributor (~INR 20-30 cr stuck flagged Nov-2025); INR 11 cr recovered, ~INR 17 cr outstanding — "not defaulted."
- **Raw-material volatility:** >100% input inflation; ability to fully reprice is the swing factor on margin.
- **Margin guidance wobble:** MD gave 30-35%, then 25-30%, then "~25% conservative" within one call — model on lower end.
- **Acquisition integration:** three acquisitions in ~12 months; consolidation of Apiqo/Bizotic minority (share swap) pending AGM.
- **Credit rating flag:** CARE marked "issuer not cooperating" (historical dispute since 2018-19, MD disputes CARE's conduct); Brickwork withdrew BB-; fresh Brickwork rating expected ~BBB- within 45 days — verify.
- **Execution dependence:** FY28 700-800 cr target needs new facility on time + working-capital funding + DMF commercializations.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Single-voice call (MD only); candid and granular on numbers, receivables, the CARE dispute, and Q4 margin causes. Some hesitancy/inconsistency on EBITDA guidance and a deferred tax-rate question (to be answered offline). Confident, slightly promotional on the FY28 doubling and acquisition cadence; anchors guidance to existing customer projections. Audio issues truncated several questions (Remember Pharma answer promised offline).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Real story is a roll-up: NSAID API specialist → backward-integrated (Bizotic/Apiqo intermediates) → forward into FDF/formulations (Remember Pharma) + CDMO + specialty chemicals — building a vertically-integrated platform, not just an API maker.
- Q4 PAT drop is largely transient cost-pass-through lag, not demand — pharma demand "increased vs pre-war"; the durable question is working capital, not the P&L.
- The genuine moat is process chemistry (methylation, Friedel-Crafts) on niche NSAIDs with only 2-3 Indian / 5-6 global players — pricing/cost edge + innovator + top-generic customers + 21 DMFs.
- A listed large pharma customer is reportedly delaying payments despite Anlon's MSME 45-day status; Anlon leverages being on the customer's DMF (hard to switch) to enforce terms — shows niche supplier stickiness.
- Microcap with stretched cash conversion entering a leveraged capex + acquisition phase — execution and WC discipline (not order book) are the binding constraints.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet was recapitalised around the 2025 BSE and NSE listing: Net Worth moves 21.03 (FY24) to 80.42 (FY25) to 254.79 (FY26) INR crore, with Other Equity rising 5.03 to 40.57 to 201.64.
- Deleveraging is pronounced - Net Debt/Equity shown as 3.55 (FY24), 0.83 (FY25), 0.17 (FY26); long-term borrowings fall 54.25 to 38.36 to 6.09 INR crore, though short-term borrowings rise 20.32 to 28.20 to 37.56.
- Returns dilute as equity expands: the metrics slide shows 13.38% / 20.82% / 15.50% and 45.92% / 25.51% / 11.42% for FY24-FY26 against labels ROCE (%) and ROE (%) in that order.
- Cash is being deployed into control stakes in three subsidiaries (INR 5.40 crore, INR 3.79 crore and INR 5.38 crore) rather than distributions - the deck states no dividend or buyback policy.
- Working capital absorbs the growth: inventories rise 41.71 to 50.26 to 113.16 INR crore and trade receivables 38.73 to 75.00 to 103.68 over FY24-FY26, against cash and bank balance of 4.37 in FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- No company-specific risk register is disclosed anywhere in the report — Risk Management is covered by a single generic paragraph — 'a well-defined risk management mechanism covering the risk mapping and trend analysis, risk exposure, potential impact and risk mitigation process is in place' — with no risk named, quantified or ranked. The Risk Management Committee met only twice in FY26 (11-11-2025 and 09-02-2026), and the Board states that 'the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report as stipulated in Section 34 of the Listing Regulations is not applicable to the Company', so the BRSR material-issues table that normally serves as an Indian issuer's risk register does not exist here. An investor has no disclosed view of what management thinks can go wrong.
- Promoter-executive sits on the committees meant to oversee him — Mr. Punitkumar Rameshbhai Rasadia is Chairman & Managing Director and is simultaneously a member of the Audit Committee and Chairman of the Risk Management Committee, and a member of the Internal Complaints Committee. Ms. Mamata Punitkumar Rasadia chairs the Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and sits on the NRC. Only two Non-Executive Independent Directors (Mr. Krishna Murty Kannepalli, Mr. Anandbhai Natwerlal Katkoria) recur across the oversight committees, so independent challenge rests on a very narrow base.
- First year as a listed company, with IPO proceeds deployment undisclosed — The Company completed its IPO during the year — a fresh issue of 1,33,00,000 equity shares at Rs.91 per share aggregating Rs.121.03 crore, listed on NSE and BSE on September 03, 2025. FY26 is therefore the first partial year of listed-company reporting, and the routed sections carry no statement on how the fresh-issue proceeds have been utilised or deviated versus objects.
- Two majority-owned subsidiaries acquired in the closing quarter, with no comparatives — The Company acquired 67.48% of Apiqo Organics Private Limited w.e.f. January 09, 2026 and 56.67% of Bizotic Life Science Private Limited w.e.f. March 20, 2026. The Board itself notes that 'comparative figure of Financial Year 2024-25 is not applicable' for the consolidated column. Both stakes are majority-but-partial, so integration execution, minority interests, and a consolidated base that reflects only weeks of ownership all sit outside any historical track record.
- Operations funded on bank cash credit and term loan facilities — Under Finance, the Board states that 'company has been utilizing cash credit/term loan facilities from the Bank and the Company has been regular in payment of interest as well as instalments as per schedule to Banks'. Working capital and expansion therefore depend on continued bank sanction and renewal; no alternative funding line, rating, or headroom is disclosed.
- No dividend, explicitly to conserve resources — 'In order to conserve resources, the Board of Directors has not recommended any dividend on the Equity Shares for the financial year.' Despite a Dividend Distribution Policy being on the books, all cash is retained, so shareholder return depends entirely on the quality of reinvestment — including into the two newly acquired subsidiaries — rather than on any payout.
- Related-party transactions in a family-held board, disclosed only by reference — Related party transactions were significant enough to require Form AOC-2 (Annexure-II), which is triggered by contracts needing disclosure, while the Board asserts all were at arm's length and in the ordinary course. Given that the Chairman & MD, a Non-Executive Director and a Whole Time Director occupy the committee seats, and that the Audit Committee that clears such transactions includes the Managing Director, the RPT stream is a structural watch item rather than a settled one.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Core NSAID APIs/intermediates:** among few Indian/global makers of Loxoprofen Sodium, Ketoprofen, Dexketoprofen Trometamol. Only ~2-3 Indian players, ~5-6 global (2 China, 1 Korea). Edge = cracked methylation / Friedel-Crafts chemistry at low landed cost; customers include innovators + top-5/10 generics.
- **Apiqo Organics (acquired ~Jan FY26):** intermediate & fine/specialty chemicals; lower EBITDA (~22-23%); near-full utilization on existing business; backward-integration intermediates to start in spare reactors → benefit from Q2 FY27. Specialty-chemical talks with 1-2 customers for dedicated capacity buyout.

business.body:
- Incorporated in 2013 and based in Rajkot, Gujarat, described as "a research-driven chemical manufacturer" of high-purity advanced pharmaceutical intermediates used as key starting materials for APIs, and of APIs that serve as raw materials for finished dosage formulations.
- Claims to be "Among the few Indian manufacturers of Loxoprofen Sodium Dihydrate, Ketoprofen & Dexketoprofen Trometamol", key APIs used for pain and inflammation, and "one of the few manufacturers of this APIs in India" for Loxoprofen Sodium Dihydrate specifically.
- "Strong global presence across 15 countries, serving pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, personal care, and animal health sectors"; 125 customers served till date (directly and indirectly) and 105 employees.
- Regulatory position framed as the moat: 21 DMFs filed with regulators across major international markets, CEP approval from EDQM (Europe) for Ketoprofen, and DMF approvals from ANVISA (Brazil) and NMPA (China) for Loxoprofen Sodium Dihydrate; DMF submissions for Ketoprofen in the USA and Dexketoprofen Trometamol in key European jurisdictions are in progress with approval "expected in a couple of years".
- Competitive edge slide cites "High Entry Barriers and Strong Quality Systems", "High-compliance manufacturing with strong DMF/GMP credentials and 33 approvals, with zero order cancellations", and 4 in-house R&D centres with QA/QC support.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Strategic initiatives slide is off-domain and unbound] The "Strategic Initiatives (Key Growth Catalysts in next 24-36 Months)" slide carries text on recycling and refurbishing spent batteries to recover Li, Co, Ni and Mn through black mass production, repairing and restoring outdated electronics for resale, environmentally responsible dismantling of obsolete electronic products, and end-to-end compliance support under E-Waste Management Rules 2022 - sitting alongside four pharma headings (Portfolio Diversification and Expansion; Expand Customer Base and Wallet Share; Improve cost management & operational efficiencies; New Product Development & DMF Filing for Regulatory). The deck does not explain the link and the text-to-heading binding is not recoverable from the extract, so no battery-recycling or e-waste business is asserted here.
- [Business model shift] The Remember India acquisition is framed as a "Transition from an API-focused manufacturer to an integrated pharmaceutical company" with entry into FDFs and "Presence across B2B APIs, domestic retail and hospital markets" - a change in business model, not just capacity.
- [Customer concentration disclosure] Top 5 and Top 10 customer revenue is disclosed only by segment split, not as a share of total revenue: FY26 slices 28.43% / 69.10% / 2.47% (Top 5) and 28.42% / 69.40% / 2.18% (Top 10), and Q1FY27 43.41% / 43.87% / 5.58% (Top 5) and 47.47% / 43.93% / 5.58% (Top 10) against labels APIs / Pharmaceutical Intermediate / Nutraceutical; label-to-value binding is again not recoverable, and the deck never states what proportion of revenue the top customers represent.
- [Stale forward-looking text] The "Future Growth Roadmap for APIs" slide, in a presentation for Q1 FY-27, still says the APIs-intermediates mix "will be driving stronger revenue momentum in FY26" and calls the initiative "a clear near-term growth catalyst for FY26 and beyond" - the horizon appears carried over from an earlier deck.

deepdive.thesis: Anlon delivered a strong FY26 (total income +43% to INR 172 cr, EBITDA +48% to INR 47.8 cr, PAT +42% to INR 29.1 cr) and bolted on three acquisitions (Apiqo, Bizotic, and FY27's Remember Pharma) to build a backward-integrated NSAID-API + intermediates + CDMO + formulations platform — but Q4 PAT fell YoY (INR 11.1 cr vs INR 16.7 cr) as a raw-material/solvent cost spike ("war situation", prices >2x) hit B2B contracts already priced at old rates, compressing margins. The story now hinges on (a) repricing customers and restoring the ~25-30% EBITDA band, (b) ramping consolidated capacity (1,400-1,600 MTPA) plus a new INR 130 cr Rajkot greenfield (commissioning ~Q1 FY28) toward a 30% revenue CAGR (FY27 ~INR 380-400 cr, FY28 ~INR 700-800 cr), and (c) fixing a stretched working-capital cycle (receivables ~200+ days, consolidated cash flow at -INR 47 cr).

Ketoprofen DMF in the US, being filed by a customer on Anlon's behalf, expected around Q2 FY27 though it may slip to Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Expects to liquidate roughly 20-25% of inventory by Q2 FY27 as acquired Apiqo/Bizotic stock is sold.
Has applied for a fresh Brickwork credit rating and expects at least BBB- within about 45 days, after both CARE and Brickwork issued issuer-not-cooperating/withdrawal remarks.

Developing three molecules for two global innovators; first molecule's commercial supply expected by Q3 FY27 and the other two to complete validation by Q2 FY27 with commercialization by Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28.
Target to become debt-free by Q3FY27 (last quarter of next calendar year); only ~4.5 CR term loan outstanding.
Plans to file three to five additional DMFs in FY27 to deepen regulated-market penetration.
Guides FY27 consolidated revenue of approximately INR 380-400 crore, backed by clear order-book visibility of INR 280-300 crore plus expected additional INR 80-90 crore.
Aims to maintain consolidated EBITDA margin in the 25-30% range, framed conservatively as ~25% sustainable and pledged not to sell below a level that would push margin under 25%.
Expects FY27 PAT of approximately INR 45 crore on a conservative basis, agreeing a realistic figure could cross INR 50-55 crore.
Funds the ~INR 130 crore capex via a term loan of INR 65-70 crore (about 50-60%) plus internal accruals, with no equity dilution planned.
Plans to launch seven new APIs in FY27 across additional therapeutic categories.
Expects positive operating/consolidated cash flow on an annual basis by end of FY27, after tightening credit terms and recovering delayed receivables.
Targets around 60% export revenue contribution in FY27.
Expects five to seven of its 21 DMF products to be commercialized in regulated export markets within FY27.
Expects receivable days to settle at least around 180 days by end of FY27 (from current elevated 200+ days).
Inorganic acquisition size estimated at INR 50-55 crore, funded from internal accruals without debt.
Planned capex of at least INR 32 crore for the greenfield expansion, funded from IPO proceeds.

wtt.tone_latest: Confident and bullish on revenue/order visibility; management explicitly owned the Q4 EBITDA/PAT miss, attributing it to war-driven raw-material cost inflation and higher operating cost from two acquisitions, while staying guarded on margins given daily raw-material price volatility.

rows.quant: Rs 116.52 cr for the Apiqo leg; ~15.4% of mcap
rows.text: acquires **44.94% of Apiqo Organics for Rs 116.52 crore** and **47.41% of Bizotic Lifescience**, both discharged by issuing **8,58,83,617 new shares at Rs 17.85** — no cash leaves the company

meta.thesis: Anlon delivered a strong FY26 (total income +43% to INR 172 cr, EBITDA +48% to INR 47.8 cr, PAT +42% to INR 29.1 cr) and bolted on three acquisitions (Apiqo, Bizotic, and FY27's Remember Pharma) to build a backward-integrated NSAID-API + intermediates + CDMO + formulations platform — but Q4 PAT fell YoY (INR 11.1 cr vs INR 16.7 cr) as a raw-material/solvent cost spike ("war situation", prices >2x) hit B2B contracts already priced at old rates, compressing margins. The story now hinges on (a) repricing customers and restoring the ~25-30% EBITDA band, (b) ramping consolidated capacity (1,400-1,600 MTPA) plus a new INR 130 cr Rajkot greenfield (commissioning ~Q1 FY28) toward a 30% revenue CAGR (FY27 ~INR 380-400 cr, FY28 ~INR 700-800 cr), and (c) fixing a stretched working-capital cycle (receivables ~200+ days, consolidated cash flow at -INR 47 cr).
